questions.question: Down's syndrome in humans is caused by
options: Presence of an extra X chromosome in a male

solution.key_concept: Down's syndrome is an autosomal aneuploidy: trisomy of chromosome 21.
steps: Down's syndrome has an extra copy of chromosome 21, giving 47 chromosomes.
Chromosome 21 is an autosome, so the condition occurs in both sexes.
solution.why_not_others: Absence of one X is Turner's syndrome. An extra X in a male is Klinefelter's syndrome. Failure of cytokinesis causes polyploidy, not trisomy.
solution.common_trap: Treating Down's syndrome as a sex-chromosome defect.

questions.question: The total chromosome number in a person with Turner's syndrome and in a person with Klinefelter's syndrome is, respectively,

solution.key_concept: Turner's syndrome is 45, XO and Klinefelter's syndrome is 47, XXY.
steps: Turner's syndrome: 44 autosomes + X = 45 chromosomes.
Klinefelter's syndrome: 44 autosomes + XXY = 47 chromosomes.
solution.why_not_others: 47 and 45 reverses the two conditions. 46 is the normal number and fits neither syndrome.
solution.common_trap: Thinking Turner's syndrome involves an extra chromosome, when it is actually a monosomy.
solution.time_saving_tip: XO means one chromosome missing (45); XXY means one extra (47).

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of Down's syndrome?
options: Furrowed tongue and partially open mouth

solution.key_concept: Each chromosomal disorder has its own set of characteristic features.
steps: Down's syndrome features: short stature, small round head, furrowed tongue, partially open mouth, palm crease, and retarded physical, psychomotor and mental development.
Overall masculine development with gynaecomastia is a feature of Klinefelter's syndrome (XXY).
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Overall masculine development with gynaecomastia
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 3 are all listed features of Down's syndrome.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the features of Down's and Klinefelter's syndromes.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Turner's syndrome is an example of aneuploidy.
statements.R: Turner's syndrome results from the presence of an additional X chromosome.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Aneuploidy is the gain or loss of a chromosome. Turner's syndrome is the loss of one X (45, XO).
steps: Turner's syndrome involves the loss of one chromosome, so it is aneuploidy. A is true.
It is caused by the absence of one X chromosome, not an extra one. R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options 1, 2 and 4 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Calling Turner's syndrome a trisomy.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: A person with Klinefelter's syndrome has 44 autosomes and an XO sex chromosome complement.
statements.II: Failure of chromatids to segregate during cell division leads to polyploidy, which is common in plants.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Klinefelter's is 44 + XXY. Non-disjunction causes aneuploidy, while failure of cytokinesis causes polyploidy.
steps: 44 + XO is Turner's syndrome; Klinefelter's is 44 + XXY. So I is incorrect.
Failure of chromatid segregation causes aneuploidy. Polyploidy comes from failure of cytokinesis after telophase. So II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Each statement contains a factual error, so every option that calls either statement correct is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Accepting II because polyploidy really is common in plants, while missing that its stated cause is wrong.

questions.question: The scientists who gave biochemical proof that the transforming principle is DNA were

solution.key_concept: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty purified cell components and identified DNA as the transforming principle.
steps: Griffith discovered transformation but could not identify the transforming principle.
Avery, MacLeod and McCarty (1933-44) showed biochemically that it is DNA.
solution.why_not_others: Hershey and Chase used bacteriophages. Meselson and Stahl proved semiconservative replication.
solution.common_trap: Crediting Griffith with identifying DNA.

questions.question: In the experiments of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty, transformation of R strain bacteria was prevented by treatment with

solution.key_concept: Only destroying DNA stopped transformation, which showed that DNA is the transforming principle.
steps: Proteases and RNases did not stop transformation.
DNase digested the DNA and blocked transformation.
solution.why_not_others: Protease and RNase, used alone or together, left DNA intact, so transformation still occurred.
solution.common_trap: Assuming protein is the hereditary material.

questions.question: In the Hershey and Chase experiment, radioactive sulphur ($^{35}S$) was used to label the bacteriophage because
options: Sulphur is present in protein but absent in DNA
Sulphur is present in DNA but absent in protein
Sulphur is present in both DNA and protein

solution.key_concept: Protein has sulphur but no phosphorus; DNA has phosphorus but no sulphur.
steps: $^{35}S$ therefore labels only the protein coat.
$^{32}P$ labels only the DNA.
Only $^{32}P$ entered the bacteria, which proved that DNA is the genetic material.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Sulphur is present in protein but absent in DNA
solution.why_not_others: DNA lacks sulphur, so options 2 and 3 are wrong. DNA contains phosphorus, so option 4 is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Swapping which isotope labels DNA and which labels protein.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Discovery of transformation in Streptococcus pneumoniae

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Biochemical proof that the transforming principle is DNA

solution.key_concept: Each milestone in the search for the genetic material belongs to a specific worker or molecule.
steps: Griffith discovered transformation using S and R strains: A-I.
Avery, MacLeod and McCarty proved the transforming principle is DNA: B-II.
Hershey and Chase used $^{32}P$ and $^{35}S$ labelled phages: C-III.
RNA was the first genetic material (RNA world): D-IV.
solution.why_not_others: The other matchings swap the contributions of Griffith, Avery and colleagues, and Hershey-Chase.
solution.common_trap: Assigning the identification of DNA to Griffith.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the genetic material are correct?

statements.A: DNA is more stable than RNA because it lacks the 2'-OH group.
statements.B: RNA mutates at a faster rate, which suits RNA viruses.
statements.C: The presence of thymine instead of uracil adds to the stability of DNA.
statements.D: Griffith identified DNA as the transforming principle.

solution.key_concept: DNA's stability comes from lacking the 2'-OH group and having thymine. RNA is reactive and mutates faster.
steps: A is correct: the 2'-OH makes RNA more reactive.
B is correct: faster mutation suits RNA viruses.
C is correct: thymine in place of uracil adds stability.
D is wrong: Griffith did not identify the transforming principle.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, B and C only
solution.why_not_others: Options 3 and 4 include the false statement D. Option 1 leaves out the true statement C.
solution.common_trap: Giving Griffith credit for identifying DNA.

questions.question: In the Watson-Crick model of DNA, guanine pairs with cytosine through

solution.key_concept: A pairs with T through 2 hydrogen bonds; G pairs with C through 3.
steps: G and C are joined by three hydrogen bonds.
solution.why_not_others: Two hydrogen bonds is the A=T pair. One and four do not occur in Watson-Crick pairing.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the A-T and G-C bond numbers.

questions.question: A double-stranded DNA sample contains 20% adenine. The percentage of cytosine in it is

solution.key_concept: Chargaff's rule: A = T and G = C in double-stranded DNA.
solution.why_not_others: 20% assumes C = A. 80% is 100 - A. 60% is G + C together, not C alone.
solution.common_trap: Forgetting to divide G + C by 2.

questions.question: The length of a double-stranded DNA molecule containing $5 \times 10^6$ base pairs is

solution.key_concept: $L = \text{bp} \times 0.34 \times 10^{-9}$ m
steps: $L = 5 \times 10^6 \times 0.34 \times 10^{-9}$ m
solution.why_not_others: $1.7 \times 10^{-2}$ m uses the pitch of 3.4 nm per bp instead of 0.34 nm. $3.4 \times 10^{-3}$ m counts both strands separately. $1.7 \times 10^{-4}$ m is a power-of-ten error.
solution.common_trap: Using 3.4 nm (the pitch of one turn) as the distance per base pair.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: In eukaryotes, negatively charged DNA wraps around the histone octamer to form a nucleosome.
statements.R: Histones are rich in acidic amino acids and are therefore negatively charged.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Histones are positively charged because they are rich in the basic amino acids lysine and arginine.
steps: DNA wraps around the histone octamer to form a nucleosome. A is true.
Histones are rich in lysine and arginine and are positively charged. R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options 1, 2 and 4 are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Forgetting that the binding depends on opposite charges.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Euchromatin is densely packed, stains dark and is transcriptionally inactive.
statements.II: The histone octamer consists of two molecules each of H1, H2A, H2B and H3.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Euchromatin is loose and active. The octamer is two each of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4, and H1 is the linker histone.
steps: Statement I describes heterochromatin, not euchromatin, so it is incorrect.
The octamer contains H4, not H1, so II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Both statements contain errors, so the other three options fail.
solution.common_trap: Including H1 in the histone octamer.

questions.question: Meselson and Stahl's experiment with E. coli proved that DNA replication is

solution.key_concept: Each daughter duplex has one parental and one new strand.
steps: After one generation in $^{14}N$, all DNA was hybrid.
This result fits semiconservative replication.
solution.why_not_others: Conservative replication would give heavy and light DNA, not hybrid. Dispersive replication was not supported. Synthesis is continuous on the leading strand.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the mode of replication with leading/lagging strand synthesis.

questions.question: E. coli cells fully labelled with $^{15}N$ are transferred to a $^{14}N$ medium and allowed to divide for 60 minutes (generation time 20 minutes). The DNA extracted would be

solution.key_concept: Fraction of hybrid DNA after n generations = $\frac{2}{2^n}$.
steps: 60 minutes / 20 minutes = 3 generations.
Hybrid fraction = $\frac{2}{2^3} = \frac{1}{4}$ = 25%.
The remaining 75% is light DNA.
solution.why_not_others: 50:50 is the result after 40 minutes. 100% hybrid is after 20 minutes. 12.5% uses $\frac{1}{2^n}$ instead of $\frac{2}{2^n}$.
solution.common_trap: Using $\frac{1}{2^n}$ instead of $\frac{2}{2^n}$.
solution.time_saving_tip: The two hybrid molecules persist; only the total number doubles each generation.

questions.question: Okazaki fragments are formed during DNA replication because
options: DNA polymerase can polymerise nucleotides only in the $5' \rightarrow 3'$ direction
DNA ligase can act only on the leading strand
DNA polymerase can initiate replication on its own
The template of the lagging strand runs $3' \rightarrow 5'$

solution.key_concept: Polymerisation only in the $5' \rightarrow 3'$ direction forces discontinuous synthesis on one strand.
steps: The leading strand (template $3' \rightarrow 5'$) is synthesised continuously.
On the other strand, synthesis happens in short pieces (Okazaki fragments), which DNA ligase joins.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): DNA polymerase can polymerise nucleotides only in the $5' \rightarrow 3'$ direction
solution.why_not_others: Ligase joins Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand. DNA polymerase cannot initiate replication on its own. The $3' \rightarrow 5'$ template belongs to the leading strand.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up which template orientation gives continuous synthesis.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Substrate and energy source for polymerisation

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Semiconservative replication shown in Vicia faba

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Heavy nitrogen source for E. coli

solution.key_concept: Each enzyme, substrate and tracer has a defined role in replication or in its experimental proof.
steps: DNA ligase joins Okazaki fragments: A-II.
dNTPs act as substrates and energy source: B-I.
$^{15}NH_4Cl$ supplied heavy nitrogen in the Meselson-Stahl experiment: C-IV.
Taylor used radioactive thymidine in Vicia faba: D-III.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps A and B. Option 2 swaps C and D. Option 4 swaps B and C.
solution.common_trap: Forgetting that dNTPs also supply the energy for polymerisation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about DNA replication are correct?

statements.A: E. coli replicates its DNA at a rate of roughly 2000 bp per second.
statements.B: In eukaryotes, DNA replication takes place in the S phase.
statements.C: Synthesis is continuous on the strand whose template runs $3' \rightarrow 5'$.
statements.D: DNA polymerase can initiate the synthesis of a new strand on its own.
statements.E: Failure of cell division after DNA replication results in polyploidy.

options: A, B, C and E only
B, C, D and E only
A, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: Facts about the rate, timing and direction of replication, and what follows if division fails.
steps: A is true: $4.6 \times 10^6$ bp in about 18 minutes is roughly 2000 bp per second.
B is true: replication occurs in the S phase.
C is true: the leading strand template runs $3' \rightarrow 5'$.
D is false: DNA polymerase cannot initiate replication on its own.
E is true: replication without division leads to polyploidy.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, B, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 3 and 4 include the false statement D. Option 1 leaves out the true statement E.
solution.common_trap: Believing that DNA polymerase can start synthesis by itself.
solution.time_saving_tip: Spot D as false first; only options 1 and 2 remain, and E is true.
